A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GSLoc research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved from v1's supplement into v2's main text.

before.justification: V1 reports original localization experiments on 7Scenes, 12Scenes, and Cambridge Landmarks, runtime measurements, matcher and ACT ablations, and supplementary ground-truth and iteration studies.

after.justification: V2 retains original localization experiments, runtime measurements, and ablations, with revised numerical results and additional qualitative segmentation and retrieval comparisons.

M1.justification: V2 removes the optional iterative feedback procedure described in v1 Section 3.2 and drawn in its pipeline figures, retaining single-pass refinement. The underlying 3DGS, ACT, MASt3R, PnP/RANSAC, and GSLocrel components remain unchanged; newly disclosed reconstruction details do not establish a new core algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three localization benchmarks and indoor/outdoor scene coverage. Added masking and retrieval illustrations concern existing scenes. Removing dSLAM-based localization results changes ground-truth evaluation coverage, rather than the represented environments or localization task.

E2.justification: V2 adds pNeRFLoc to the 7Scenes comparison, PMNet to Cambridge, and a qualitative NetVLAD retrieval comparison. It drops supplementary sequential-APR comparisons involving VLocNet, MapNet+PGO, AtLoc+, and TransAPR variants. MCLoc was already compared in v1's appendix; its main-text appearance is principally relocation.

E3.justification: V2 adds a 2cm/2° recall threshold for 7Scenes and mask/ACT controls for qualitative rendering comparisons. Main DFNet results emphasize one-step refinement, already tested in v1 Table 13, while two-step controls and dSLAM localization evaluation disappear. The stated image resolutions, training budget, and default SfM ground truth remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 removes the iteration/convergence study in v1 Section 8 and Table 13 and the localization sensitivity comparison between dSLAM and SfM poses in Table 11. It adds mask/ACT rendering comparisons and a retrieval-versus-rendering overlap case study in Figures 9–10. Matcher and ACT ablations and the ground-truth rendering-quality comparison remain.

E5.justification: Both runtime sections state that measurements are averaged over 1,000 runs. Neither version reports localization seed variation, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests; v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Reported one-shot DFNet+GSLoc error on 7Scenes changes from 4.0cm/1.0° in v1 Table 13 to 1.1cm/0.34° in v2 Table 1. Marepo+GSLoc's 12Scenes recall changes from 70.3% to 90.9%, and NeRFMatch's 7Scenes recall from 75.4% to 78.4%. Matcher-ablation scores also change, stricter recall results are added, and supplementary result entries disappear. These are revised reports, without an established explanation for all underlying experimental differences.

T1.justification: The ACT transformation, Gaussian depth-rendering expression, and relative-pose composition equations remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. The removed 'Accuracy Bound' section reports empirical iteration behavior rather than a mathematical bound.

C1.justification: V2 strengthens the efficiency claim to one-shot refinement, including outperforming NeFeS with DFNet on 7Scenes, where v1 said two rounds were needed. The central contributions and claims about improving APR/SCR localization and achieving leading indoor accuracy otherwise retain their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 adds substantive arguments about feature-map information loss, one matching operation versus HLoc's multiple retrieved images, and greater query overlap from rendered views. V2 removes v1's discussion of iteration-dependent convergence and the relationship between initial-pose accuracy and refined accuracy. The limitation that GSLocrel degrades accurate ACE estimates remains.

D1.justification: V2 Appendix A.1 newly identifies prebuilt COLMAP/HLoc model sources and describes using dataset depth maps and rendered depth to improve the 7Scenes sparse point cloud. V1 specified COLMAP sparse initialization without these details. This improves disclosure but does not establish when the procedure was introduced. Hardware, training iterations, resizing, ACT settings, and the project-page address remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds literature on PMNet, pNeRFLoc, parallel NeRF inversion, image-retrieval benchmarking, LaMAR, and Air-HLoc. References supporting removed sequential-APR comparisons disappear, as does the DUSt3R reference despite retaining that matcher. Appendix A.3 expands positioning against retrieval and rendering-based approaches, while the main related-work framework remains similar.

P1.justification: V2 edits the introduction, shortens the conclusion, swaps the Cambridge and 12Scenes discussion order, and reorganizes the supplement into Appendix A.1–A.4. One-shot terminology replaces iteration-specific language. Most main-text organization and method exposition remain closely matched.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document from two columns to one, adds a front-page teaser, redraws pipeline diagrams without iterative feedback, merges the GSLocrel comparison tables, and transposes runtime and matcher tables. It adds segmentation and retrieval figures and reorganizes qualitative examples; Figure 11 partly redisplays examples already present in v1.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful reconstruction details, stricter 7Scenes evaluation, and visual evidence about masking. However, its appendix removes quantitative evidence about convergence and sensitivity to ground-truth poses. Large revised indoor scores, including Marepo's 12Scenes recall changing from 70.3% to 90.9%, lack a clear accompanying explanation of procedural changes. The gains in documentation and evaluation detail coexist with losses in diagnostic evidence, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
